body.p: This responds to the Final Office Action dated February 16, 2022.

Claims 20-22, 24 and 25 are presently amended. Claims 1-19 and 26-78 were previously withdrawn and are presently canceled. New claims 79-84 are presently added. As a result, claims 20-25 and 79-84 are now pending in this application.

Claims 79-84 are new. Support for the new claims may be found in the specification as- filed, such as at paragraphs [0130], [0211], [0219], [0237], and [0257]. Applicant believes that no new matter has been introduced in the added claims. Additionally, for at least the reasons discussed below, Applicant respectfully submits that the new claims are patentably distinct over the references currently cited as a basis of rejection, Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner consider and allow the newly added claims.
Claims 20 and 22-24 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Bohm Sebastian (U.S. 2012/0078071). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 20 recites,
an implantable analyte sensor configured to continuously monitor at least
a sensor mounting unit, the implantable analyte sensor coupled to the
sensor mounting unit; and
an adhesive pad coupled to the sensor mounting unit to adhere the sensor
mounting unit to a skin surface of a host; and
a first heating element included in the adhesive pad and positioned to
provide heat to the skin surface of the host when the implantable analyte sensor is
inserted into the host.
Applicant submits no new matter is added, and that support for the amendments may be found in the specification as originally filed, including at least paragraphs [0164] and [0165].

The Final Office Action concedes "Bohm does not explicitly disclose the first heating element included in the adhesive pad." Final Office Action at p. 5. The Final Office Action alleges, "[t]here are limited places where the heating element could be placed and a person having ordinary skill in the

art would be motivated to find the best and most convenient places." Id. Applicant respectfully disagrees. Bohm does not contemplate having a heating element being included in an adhesive pad. Rather, the portions of Bohm relied upon by the Examiner, paragraphs [0143] and [0273], discuss, respectively, the mounting unit and that the position of a heating element may be either in vivo or ex vivo. Bohm discusses adhesive pads as well, without contemplating the positioning of a heating element included therein. Bohm at [0143], [0273]. For example, Bohm discusses a temperature sensor or thermal conductive material being included in the adhesive pad, which is not the same as, nor does it teach or suggest or otherwise render obvious the first heating element of claim 20. Id. at [0256], [0259]. However, Bohm is silent as to a first heating element included in the adhesive pad and positioned to provide heat to the skin surface of the host when the implantable analyte sensor is inserted into the host, as recited in claim 20.

Applicant respectfully submits that Bohm does not teach, suggest, nor render obvious claim 20. Claims 22-24 depend from claim 20. Withdrawal of the rejection of claims 20 and 22-24 is respectfully requested.
Dependent claim 23 is rejected over Bohm. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claim 23 recites,
wherein the sensor electronics hardware is configured to perform
operations comprising:
detecting that the implantable analyte sensor has been inserted into a host;
beginning to provide power to the first heating element; and
after a first time period, ceasing to provide power to the first heating
element.

The Final Office Action relies on the same paragraphs of Bohm discussed above with respect to claim 20 to reject claim 23. Applicant respectfully submits that claim 23 is allowable at least because of its dependance on claim 20.

Further, Bohm does not teach, suggest, nor render obvious claim 23. For example, paragraph [0143] discusses the construction of the mounting unit, but is silent as to detecting that the implantable analyte sensor has been inserted into a host and beginning to provide power to the first heating element, much less after a first time period, ceasing to provide power to the first heating element, as recited in claim 20. Bohm at [0143]. For example, Bohm discusses using a temperature sensor, "as

an indicator that the sensor electronics module 12 is attached to mounting unit 240 and/or that the mounting unit is attached to the skin and/or that the sensor is implanted in the host. Id. at [0262]. Accordingly, Bohm does not teach, suggest, nor render obvious detecting that the implantable analyte sensor has been inserted into a host and beginning to provide power to the first heating element, and, after a first time period, ceasing to provide power to the first heating element, as recited in claim 20.
Withdrawal of the rejection of claim 23 is respectfully requested.

Claim 21 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Bohm (U.S. 2012/0078071) in view of Burkett (U.S. 5918590). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claim 21 depends from claim 20. Bohm is discussed above with respect to claim 20. Applicant respectfully submits that Burkett, alone or in combination with Bohm, does not teach, suggest, or otherwise render claim 25 obvious. Withdrawal of the rejection of claim 21 is respectfully requested.

Claim 25 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Bohm (U.S. 2012/0078071) in view of Lee (U.S. 2016/0058380). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claim 25 depends from claim 20. Bohm is discussed above with respect to claim 20. Applicant respectfully submits that Lee, alone or in combination with Bohm, does not teach, suggest, or otherwise render claim 25 obvious. Withdrawal of the rejection of claim 25 is respectfully requested.

In the interest of clarity and brevity, every assertion made in the Office Action may not have been equally addressed. Silence regarding any such assertion does not constitute any admission or acquiescence. All rights not exercised in connection with this response, such as the right to challenge or rebut any tacit or explicit characterization of any reference or of any of the present claims, the right to challenge or rebut any asserted factual or legal basis of any of the rejections, the right to swear behind any cited reference such as provided under 37 C.F.R. § 1.131 or otherwise, or the right to assert co-ownership of any cited reference, are reserved. It is not admitted that any of the cited references or any other references of record are relevant to the present claims, or that they constitute prior art. To the extent that any rejection or assertion is based upon the Examiner's personal knowledge, rather than any objective evidence of record as manifested by a cited prior art

reference, timely objection to such reliance on Official Notice is made, and all rights to request that the Examiner provide a reference or affidavit in support of such assertion, as required by MPEP § 2144.03, are reserved. All rights to pursue any cancelled claims in a subsequent patent application claiming the benefit of priority of the present patent application, and to request rejoinder of any withdrawn claim, as required by MPEP § 821.04, are likewise reserved.

It is respectfully submitted that the claims are in condition for allowance, and notification to that effect is earnestly requested. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at (612) 373-6900 to facilitate prosecution of this application.
If necessary, please charge any additional fees or deficiencies, or credit any overpayments to Deposit Account No. 19-0743.
